name: Benzodiazepine conversion
seoDesc: Benzodiazepine conversion: work out alprazolam (Xanax) from the bromazepam. A free health calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The Benzodiazepine conversion calculator returns alprazolam (Xanax) from the field on the form. No sign-up, no page reload, and the relationship behind it is printed below. That makes it useful for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the Benzodiazepine conversion calculator work?
sections.html:
The Benzodiazepine conversion calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports alprazolam (Xanax) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the bromazepam (Lexotan).

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html: • A measured quantity, entered by default in milligrams. The unit chip switches it to any of the 29 supported units.

sections.title: The formula behind the Benzodiazepine conversion calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Alprazolam (Xanax)=(1 ÷ 6) × bromazepam (Lexotan)
Alprazolam (Xanax)=(1 ÷ 50) × chlordiazepoxide (Librium)
Alprazolam (Xanax)=clonazepam (Rivotril)
Alprazolam (Xanax)=(1 ÷ 20) × clorazepate (Tranxene)
Alprazolam (Xanax)=(1 ÷ 30) × flurazepam (Dalmane)
Alprazolam (Xanax)=(1 ÷ 2) × lorazepam (Ativan)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Suppose Bromazepam (Lexotan) = 10 mg. Working through the relationship above gives Midazolam IV (Versed) = 6.6667 mg, Midazolam PO = 16.6667 mg, Oxazepam (Serax) = 50 mg and Secobarbital (Seconal) = 166.6667 mg.

The point of the example is the scale, not the particular digits: swap in your own figures and the same relationship produces your answer.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Midazolam IV (Versed) = 6.6667 mg, Midazolam PO = 16.6667 mg, Oxazepam (Serax) = 50 mg and Secobarbital (Seconal) = 166.6667 mg should be roughly the size you expected from Bromazepam (Lexotan) = 10 mg.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Benzodiazepine conversion calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Any time the same 1 figures keep coming back — the bromazepam — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html: • Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.

faq.q: What does the Benzodiazepine conversion calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns alprazolam (Xanax), derived from the bromazepam. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Benzodiazepine conversion calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the bromazepam, which is 1 field in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter midazolam IV (Versed) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Midazolam IV (Versed) opens in milligrams and the chip beside it offers 29 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Midazolam IV (Versed) = 6.6667 mg. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Benzodiazepine conversion calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
